A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UnmaskingTrees/BaltoBot work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched across reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v4 reports original generation, imputation, probabilistic prediction, and M5 forecasting experiments, with ablations and per-dataset results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the proposed methods' benchmark scores, synthetic examples, ablations, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 revises feature routing: v4 assigns continuous features to BaltoBot and everything else to XGBClassifier; v5 assigns categorical features to XGBClassifier and everything else to BaltoBot. This changes the stated routing for non-categorical discrete features. The remaining algorithm steps are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 27-dataset imputation/generation benchmark, Two Moons and Iris examples, wave and Poisson prediction tasks, and M5 forecasting. Complete-data and missing-data scenarios are retained; shortened dataset labels in Table 7 do not change coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding benchmarks and case studies, including the ForestDiffusion variants and Table 5's Treeffuser, Deep Ensembles, IBUG, NGBoost Poisson, and Quantile Regression Forests comparisons. Newly discussed methods such as Tabsyn are not added to the evaluations.

E3.justification: The benchmark missingness conditions, H = 4 and K = 50, and M5 data sizes, sampling procedures, splits, and tuning budget are retained. v5's explanation of how H was selected documents existing tuning rather than reporting a changed evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The k-Means/KDI/BaltoBot ablations in Tables 2 and 6, synthetic case studies, and runtime analyses are retained. The new discussion of tree-height tradeoffs introduces no sensitivity experiment or additional analysis results.

E5.justification: The benchmark reporting retains three experiments per dataset, ten imputations per imputation experiment, and the same standard-error reporting. No seed information, repeated-run counts, or statistical testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical rows in Tables 1–10 match after accounting for abbreviated dataset labels. Figures 1–5 retain the same plotted results, and the corresponding empirical findings and rankings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 adds an O(ND^2) complexity argument for MissForest and MICE-Forest, assuming iteration counts do not depend on dataset size. Section 4 adds the cubic-versus-quadratic feature-scaling comparison for UnmaskingTrees and ForestDiffusion. Existing mathematical formulations remain unchanged, with no new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction qualify performance claims as out-of-the-box results on 27 small datasets and describe imputation performance as leading rather than state-of-the-art. The conclusion also drops its explicit state-of-the-art sales-forecasting claim, while retaining the core methodological contributions.

C2.justification: Beyond v4's benchmark weaknesses and TabPFN memory limitations, v5 adds substantive limitations concerning tree-height selection, training-time/diversity tradeoffs, cubic feature scaling, and applicability to small datasets with limited resources. Sections 2.2 and 5 also expand the explanations for KDI's suitability and diffusion's advantages.

D1.justification: Section 3 newly explains that tree height was increased on Two Moons and Iris until the plots stopped showing visible improvement; v4 only stated that these examples were used for tuning. Reported hyperparameter values, hardware, and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds missing-data foundations and application references, Liao et al. on masked language modeling, and connections to Tabsyn, scalable tree-based diffusion, optimized feature orderings, and hierarchical softmax. These broaden the background and future-work context while preserving the central positioning against existing tabular generation methods.

P1.justification: v5 expands the introduction, reorganizes the method's explanatory prose, integrates Algorithms 1–3 into Section 2, and expands Section 4 into Limitations and Future Work. Terminology, publication information, and cross-references receive targeted edits; most existing prose and the main section order remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is retypeset throughout in TMLR format, changing typography, text width, and float placement. Algorithms move into the main text, figures and appendix tables are regrouped, and Table 10 is separated from Figure 5. Table 1 loses its metric explanations and Table 7 abbreviates labels, while plotted content and table structures remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 better aligns its headline claims with the small, out-of-the-box benchmark and makes important scalability, tree-height, and applicability limitations explicit. The added tuning explanation improves transparency. These provide a limited net improvement despite the loss of useful metric explanations from Table 1; the empirical evidence itself is unchanged.
